title: podman machine: `exec format error` when running arches other than arm/x86
body:
### Issue Description

I am using podman that was installed with podman desktop (6.0.2) after upgrading from 5.x

This version of podman doesn't seem to run any emulated containers anymore (see below). I've also tried recreating the podman machine from scratch and it's the same results.

but, for example, s390x and ppc64le don't work:

```
{
  "msg": "exec container process `\/bin\/uname`: Exec format error",

```

qemu-user-static looks like it's already installed, but I've tried older tricks such as 
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27364#issuecomment-3549067472, and all it seems to do is break the rpm-ostreed service.

I've also tried the tried and true `podman run --rm --privileged tonistiigi/binfmt --install all`, and while that appears to complete, it doesn't work. I assume the bootc readonly fs is somehow contributing here.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create a podman machine on macOS (I used `podman machine init --cpus 6 --memory 8192 --disk-size 150 --now`)
2. `podman run --rm --platform linux/s390x alpine uname -a`

### Describe the results you received

```json
{
  "msg": "exec container process `\/bin\/uname`: Exec format error",
  "level": "error",
  "time": "2026-08-31T18:57:55.811772Z"
}
```

### Describe the results you expected

The output of `uname -a` from that container.

### Additional information

I do see that in podman info it says

```
  emulatedArchitectures:
```

comments.body:
That is expected, we only install the arm and x86 emulation packages. 

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/blob/fe57561af3dc8ad1ce8c6b5398c9a22ae11f4bf1/podman-image/build_common.sh#L102-L104

this is also not new, the packages were reduced in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/commit/ef5d4adf9fe44e938b13644ae1365eb09dd9402d which was podman 5.6.

Adding all possible arches add a lot to the image size with no gain for the vast majority of users, so we decided the only keep x86/arm arches.

cc @baude 

Not sure if you have opinion here, we could consider adding more arches back since we removed the a while ago I guess there really is not a lot of user interest to justify that IMO.

I don't mind them not being there by default, but how do I add them back manually?

> this is also not new, the packages were reduced in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/commit/ef5d4adf9fe44e938b13644ae1365eb09dd9402d which was podman 5.6.

Right, on podman 5.6, I could add them back in rather easily with something like `rpm-ostree install qemu-user-static`. I think there was a change to a bootc based image, which is read-only, and I can't seem to add them now.

Modification is not really directly supported or recommend. I don't know if this still work but is used to be "rpm-ostree install <package>" and then reboot which could do layering but we move away from the older fedora coreos base to a bootc base where this is not a thing I believe.

I think the most stable approach would use our image as base and dnf install what you need during a container build and then bootc apply your new image with podman machine os apply for example. But then you must update your image on your own for each new podman version.

While I understand not recommending modifications to the image, emulation of other arches seems like one of those acceptable cases.

> I had tried rpm-ostree install and it just breaks the rpm-ostreed service

Ah yes this is a known issue and expected for now until it rebases to fedora 45, since we do not rpm-ostree ourselves that is not a problem for us.

I am not very familiar with bootc, so I'm certain I'm doing something wrong, but I basically tried:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM quay.io/podman/machine-os:6.0
RUN dnf -y install qemu-user-static
```

then

```sh
$ podman build -f Dockerfile.podman-bootc -t docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0
$ docker push docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0
$ podman machine init --cpus 6 --memory 8192 --disk-size 150 --image docker://docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0 --now podman-machine2
```

which errored with

```
Looking up Podman Machine image at docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0 to create VM
Error: wrong manifest type for disk artifact: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json
```

tried again with podman build `--format docker` but that errored with 

```
Looking up Podman Machine image at docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0 to create VM
Error: wrong manifest type for disk artifact: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json
```

---

I'm guessing there's some specific bootc commands I need to actually run instead, but as I'm very unfamiliar with it, I'm not sure what those are. Help?

you cannot direct boot the container image, there is a somewhat complex pipeline in podman-machine-os that turns the oci image back to VM disk images that can be booted which the podman machine init command needs.

What you need to do is init you machine as normal, and the after boot use `podman machine os apply --restart <container image>` which should apply your custom image
https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-machine-os-apply.1.html

Success!

```sh
$ podman machine init --cpus 6 --memory 8192 --disk-size 150 --now
$ podman machine os apply docker://docker.io/fryguy9/machine-os-qemu:6.0
```

I think regardless of the qemu-user-static having a documented process on how to build a custom container image and apply to to podman machine is useful.

As for location I guess a tutorial would be the best fit https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/tree/main/docs/tutorials
They should accessible on https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/Tutorials.html for people to find.

> Also, I wanted to add that adding all of the architectures added ~200MB of disk size. Not sure if that makes a big difference as the base image is already 1.78GB, so 1.97GB (~10% bigger) doesn't seem all that different to me. 🤷

10% is a lot to us. The smaller the better, there is likely much more we can improve in the image itself.
